branch_provenance.syndrome: Subacute Painful Soft Tissue Mass on the Hand of Uncertain Aetiology

state.case_summary:
A woman in her 30s presented with a painful bruise on her hand that initially appeared a few days after she sustained a twisting injury to the affected hand while participating in acroyoga 2 years before. Since the initial onset, the bruise and pain had persisted despite icing and resting the area. She denied any personal or family history of bleeding disorders.

An ill-defined indurated blue-green plaque was noted on the dorsum of the left hand.

- Radiography: Showed soft tissue swelling but were otherwise unremarkable.- Magnetic Resonance Imaging: Showed a heterogeneously fluid hyperintense and T1 heterogeneously hyperintense lesion measuring approximately 1.6 × 0.5 × 2.9 cm that was centered within the dorsal subcutaneous soft tissue of the hand.- Pathology:   - Mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition  - Lesional cells were spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid, with open chromatin, prominent nucleoli, and without mitoses  - Mixed inflammatory infiltrate including neutrophils, histiocytes, and foamy macrophages  - Immunohistochemistry: Strongly positive for CD34; negative for S100, SOX10, HMB45, and Melan-A- Images:  Title: Figure 1 - Soft green-blue plaque on the dorsal hand  Title: Figure 2A - H&E stain demonstrating spindled cells surrounding fat globules  Title: Figure 2B - High-power H&E photomicrograph demonstrating pigmented and regular spindled cells surrounding fat globules  Title: Figure 2C - Lesional cells strongly positive for CD34

What is the most likely diagnosis?

Options:
A. Hemosiderotic Dermatofibroma
B. Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans (Bednar tumor)
C. Hemosiderotic fibrolipomatous tumor (HFLT)
D. Giant cell tumor of tendon sheath

excluded_candidates: Infectious process: reason ranked lower due to lack of systemic symptoms
Malignant process: reason ranked lower due to lack of mitoses and negative immunohistochemistry for S100, SOX10, HMB45, and Melan-A
